person: Ray Okafor, 42, is project manager for a general contractor and its electrical arm. He is prime on a county-owned fire station renovation paid partly with federal-aid funds, with a four-person electrical crew that includes one registered apprentice. He does paperwork in the hour after the site closes, and a prior late notice cost his company $40,000, so he wants every filing correct and on time. Certified payroll has piled up over several weeks and the county is holding two pay estimates, so he wants Athena to work out what is owed and file only what is due.
stated_up_front: County's holding two pay estimates on the fire station job because certified payrolls are behind. Go through the weeks, tell me what's due and what's wrong with our pay, and fix it. Don't file anything I haven't seen.

facts.truth: County fire station No. 4 renovation, electrical subcontract under our GC contract, federal-aid funded, Davis-Bacon wage determination attached to the contract.
Estimate 5 ($86,400) and Estimate 6 ($92,150) are held by the county until certified payrolls are current.
Three journeyman electricians (Dale Whitfield, Marcus Ibarra, Tomas Reyes) and one registered apprentice, Kayla Brandt, in a state-registered program.
Kayla's registration says 60% of journeyman base rate in her first period, and she is paid that. Ray believes it is correct.
Week ending Sept 12: site shut for the inspection hold, nobody on the fire station, so it needs a no-work statement.
Week ending Sept 19: only Marcus was there, 6 hours pulling a permit sign-off and conduit check. That is a payroll week, not a no-work week.
Weeks ending Aug 29 and Sept 5 were accepted. Week ending Sept 26 is under review by the county.
Week ending Oct 24 is still in progress today, Oct 23, so it is not due.
The crew also does a private warehouse job where the contract rate is lower. No wage determination covers it, so those hours stay off the certified payroll.
Dale and Tomas worked 46 hours one week on the fire station and Ray believes overtime was paid at straight time on the extra hours.
Tomas spent two days on trenching and conduit pulling with a trencher, which the foreman notes as laborer-type work. Ray is unsure what rate that falls under.

unknowns: Which classification and rate the wage determination assigns to the trenching Tomas did
How much of the journeyman fringe is met by the company plan versus paid in cash
The county's deadline for filing a late certified payroll or the penalty for being late
Whether the system will accept a no-work statement for a past week
